text.p: "Sleepers" the Warner Bros. film about four boys from New York's Hell's Kitchen who are sent to reform school where they are tortured and abused, opened at the top of the weekend box office charts.

According to industry estimates released Sunday by Exhibitor Relations Inc., the Barry Levinson-directed film, which stars Brad Pitt, Dustin Hoffman, Robert De Niro and Kevin Bacon, pulled in $12.6 million over the three-day period ended Sunday.

Paramount Pictures captured the second and third spot with "The Ghost and the Darkness" grossing $7.6 million over the weekend, followed by "First Wives Club" at $7.1 million. "The Long Kiss Goodnight" by New Line Cinema came in fourth at $7.0 million.
"That Thing You Do," starring Oscar-winner Tom Hanks, pulled in $4.1 million, giving the film $18.1 million since it opened.
Rounding out the bottom five films for the weekend are: "D3: The Mighty Ducks", "The Chamber", "Get on the Bus", "The Glimmer Man" and "Fly Away Home."
Box office figures are based on actual ticket sales reports for Friday and Saturday and estimates for Sunday.
Warner Bros. is a unit of Time Warner, Paramount is a unit of Viacom Inc., and New Line is a unit of Turner Broadcasting Systems.
